record.paper_title: Kirby diagrams, trisections and gems of PL 4-manifolds: relationships, results and open problems
record.original_question: Which closed simply-connected 4-manifolds admit a gem Γ together with a cyclic ordering ε of the five colors such that the {ε_0,ε_2,ε_4}-colored subgraph and the {ε_1,ε_3,ε_4}-colored subgraph are each connected, and the decomposition T(Γ,ε) is a gem-induced trisection? More broadly, can one characterize topologically the 4-manifolds admitting gems satisfying the hypotheses of Proposition 26, or at least identify substantial classes of manifolds with this property?

evidence.quote: Proposition 26 ([10]) gT (M) = β2(M) for each closed (simply-connected) 4-manifold M which admits a 5-colored graph Γ ∈ G(4)s representing M with gε0,ε2,ε4 = 1 and gε1,ε3,ε4 = 1 (ε being a cyclic permutation of ∆4), so that T (Γ, ε) is a gem-induced trisection.
It would be very interesting to characterize topologically 4-manifolds admitting gems which satisfy the hypotheses of the above statement, or at least to find classes satisfying them.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. An (n+1)-colored graph is a pair (Γ, γ) where Γ = (V(Γ), E(Γ)) is a finite multigraph (loops forbidden) that is regular of degree n+1, and γ : E(Γ) → Δ_n := {0, 1, …, n} is an edge-coloring such that incident edges have distinct colors. For a subset B ⊆ Δ_n, let Γ_B denote the subgraph (V(Γ), γ^{-1}(B)); its connected components are called B-residues, and their number is denoted g_B.

To a colored graph one associates an n-dimensional pseudocomplex K(Γ): take an n-simplex σ_v for every v ∈ V(Γ), label its vertices by the colors in Δ_n, and for every edge of color c joining v and w glue σ_v to σ_w along their (n-1)-faces opposite to the c-labelled vertex, matching equally labelled vertices. A 5-colored graph Γ is called a gem (graph-encoded manifold) of a closed PL 4-manifold M if |K(Γ)| is PL-homeomorphic to M. Let G(4)_s denote the class of 5-colored gems whose associated complex is a closed simply-connected PL 4-manifold.

For a gem Γ ∈ G(4)_s and a cyclic ordering ε = (ε_0, ε_1, ε_2, ε_3, ε_4) of the five colors of Δ_4, one constructs a decomposition T(Γ, ε) of M into three 4-dimensional handlebody-like pieces by partitioning the colors via ε; under suitable connectedness hypotheses this decomposition is a trisection of M in the sense of Gay–Kirby, and is then called a gem-induced trisection. The trisection genus g_T(M) is the minimum genus of any trisection of M, and β_2(M) denotes the second Betti number.

Problem. Give a topological characterization of those closed simply-connected PL 4-manifolds M for which there exist a gem Γ ∈ G(4)_s representing M and a cyclic ordering ε of Δ_4 such that
  (i) the {ε_0, ε_2, ε_4}-colored subgraph Γ_{ε_0 ε_2 ε_4} is connected, i.e. g_{ε_0,ε_2,ε_4} = 1;
  (ii) the {ε_1, ε_3, ε_4}-colored subgraph Γ_{ε_1 ε_3 ε_4} is connected, i.e. g_{ε_1,ε_3,ε_4} = 1;
  (iii) the associated decomposition T(Γ, ε) is a gem-induced trisection of M.

At minimum, exhibit substantial classes of closed simply-connected 4-manifolds for which such a pair (Γ, ε) exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in the literature on gems and trisections of PL 4-manifolds. A web search did not surface any subsequent paper providing a topological characterization or a comprehensive class-level answer; related work by Casali–Cristofori and collaborators continues to study gem-induced trisections, but the characterization itself appears to remain open.
